guide.investigator_notes_fake_online_stores:
storefronts copy real-brand product pages pixel-for-pixel; prices set 35-60% below RRP.
domain age usually under 90 days; WHOIS data redacted or registered to a shell address.
payment forms accept card-only — no PayPal, no cash-on-delivery — which is the tell.
products never ship; chargeback windows close before victims realize the order is fake.
recommend: search "{domain} reviews scam" and check the site age before ordering.
guide.investigator_notes_generic:
active investigation — pattern indicators logged from open-source intelligence feeds.
victim reporting rate stays low; most cases surface only through bank-side chargeback data.
attack surface evolves faster than the typical user's threat model — refresh quarterly.
recommend: study the red flags in the body of this dossier and practice in the simulator.
guide.investigator_notes_investment_pyramids:
structure: returns paid from new-recruit deposits, not from any underlying investment.
collapse window typically 9-18 months from launch; last 30 days produce ~40% of victims.
promised returns above 20%/month should be treated as a confirmed pyramid signal.
social-proof tactics: paid testimonials, fabricated "auditor" PDFs, staged office tours.
recommend: verify the operator with the local financial regulator before any deposit.
guide.investigator_notes_nigerian_letters:
classic 419 variant — still active 30+ years after first documented case in 1992.
modern channels: Telegram DMs, LinkedIn InMail, dating apps, not the legacy email vector.
average ask escalates from $200 "courier fee" to $5,000+ across 4-6 message exchanges.
attackers operate primarily from West Africa and Eastern Europe; payouts route through crypto.
recommend: never wire money to unlock a larger sum — that is the entire scam, by definition.
guide.investigator_notes_phishing:
pattern confirmed across 47 distinct attack groups operating under spoofed bank domains.
peak window: 19:00-23:00 local time on weekdays; spikes after payroll dates.
~6% of victims contact law enforcement; most report only to the impersonated bank.
link domains rotate every 48-96h; SMS sender IDs reuse the same 12-character pool.
recommend: targeted briefings via /journal — see SMS scam newsletter.

course.bullet_practical_text: Every concept is paired with a decision you will actually face in your inbox or on your phone.
course.bullet_self_paced_text: Start any module the moment it unlocks; pick up where you left off.
course.bullet_verifiable_text: Pass the capstone simulation to earn a shareable DiScammer Defender certificate.
course.cert_text: Finish all nine modules and pass the capstone simulation to receive a shareable certificate verifying that you can recognize, respond to, and recover from modern digital fraud.
course.debrief_fallback_next_action: Mark this debrief complete, then open the next briefing or run the assessment.
course.debrief_fallback_takeaway: The pattern in this briefing rarely appears alone — expect a time-pressure trigger and an unverifiable channel alongside it.
course.faq_free_a: Yes. DiScammer is a public-interest project. We do not sell your data and we do not charge for the curriculum or the certificate.
course.faq_install_a: No. Everything runs in the browser. The simulations work on desktop and mobile, and your progress is saved automatically.
course.faq_install_q: Do I need to install anything?
course.faq_long_a: Around nine hours of focused study end to end. Most people finish over two to three weeks, one module per evening, but you can pace it however suits you.
course.faq_who_a: Anyone who uses email, a phone, or a bank account. The early modules assume zero background; the later ones go deep enough to be useful for IT and security teams.
course.intro: A structured, scenario-driven curriculum that teaches you to recognize, respond to, and recover from modern digital fraud. Each module pairs concise theory with real-world examples, hands-on exercises, and an interactive simulation.
course.lessons_empty: Lessons for this module are launching soon. Check back in a few days.
course.objectives_default_recognize: RECOGNIZE THE PATTERN IN REAL-WORLD EXAMPLES
course.section_missions_lead: Nine missions, executed in sequence. Each unlocks once the prior briefing is debriefed.
course.step_certify_text: Pass the capstone exam and three scenario simulations to earn the DiScammer Defender certificate — shareable on your résumé and LinkedIn.
course.step_learn_text: Read a concise briefing in each module — no fluff, no jargon. Every lesson opens with the question it answers and the decision it improves.
course.step_practice_text: Triage real phishing messages, evaluate suspicious stores, and respond to deepfake calls inside short, gamified simulations.
